LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Sole possession of first place in the NFC North is on the line at Ford Field as two 8-2 rivals clash on Thanksgiving with long winning streaks Imagn Images In the first of three Thanksgiving day games, the Detroit Lions play host to the division rival Chicago Bears in one of the biggest games of the NFL season to date. Detroit enters this game winners of six straight and sitting in first place in the NFC North with an 8-2 record. The Lions sport one of the NFL's most efficient and explosive offenses, and their efense hasn't allowed more than 21 points in a game since all the way back in Week 4. The Lions are dealing with injury issues on that side of the ball, but they've held up surprisingly well. That will be put to the test on Thursday afternoon. Chicago comes into this game having won five in a row and sporting an 8-2 record that matches that of Detroit, with the Bears sitting in second place in the division by virtue of a tiebreaker. The Bears also have one of the league's best offenses, while the defense has been strengthened by the acquisition of superstar defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons , who seems to have transformed the unit up front and allowed everything else to click properly into place. That unit, too, will be tested more than ever here. Which of these two teams will keep its winning streak alive and lay claim to sole possession of first place in the division? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. The Bears rank a surprising 14th in yards per play, 12th in points per drive and 15th in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. Some of that is due to the fact that Caleb Williams missed several games with a hamstring injury, but even with Williams on the field the Bears' EPA per play mark is only the equivalent of the 10th-best offense in the league. Chicago is one of the league's most run-oriented offenses, ranking ninth in the share of plays that turn into a rush attempt. But D'Andre Swift is averaging just 3.7 yards per carry and Kyle Monangai , who has been more effective (5.0 per carry) has played in only five games. The Lions have sported a top run defense this season in allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, but that defense took a couple of massive hits over the last few weeks with the losses of Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson to injury. Still, Detroit held Tampa Bay's running backs to 84 yards on 22 carries last Sunday, when Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell had previously been destroying teams on the ground. The Bears will need Swift and Monangai to find more success if they want to control the game in the fashion they have preferred since Ben Johnson became head coach last year. Chicago's passing game has been relatively inconsistent this year, as there have been times when Caleb Williams has looked like an elite quarterback and others when he has looked ordinary — sometimes within the same game. (Like the Sunday night showdown against the Buccaneers , for example.) Williams has completed 68.3% of his passes at 7.9 yards per attempt, but he's thrown only 10 touchdown passes against six interceptions. He's 11th in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, but he's been highly susceptible against the blitz: he ranks fourth in EPA against four-man rushes but only checks in 19th when opponents rush five or more. Detroit has blitzed at a below-average rate this season (30.3%, per Tru Media), but would be wise to turn up the pressure a bit against a quarterback who has shown that he can be pressured into some bad decisions on occasion if you get defenders into his lap. Still, the Lions have been highly susceptible to opposing passing attacks, even if they have been improved since the return of Brian Branch and should get another lift as Kerby Joseph rounds into form. The Lions are 27th in EPA per dropback allowed, and they're in the bottom third in opponents' explosive play rate through the air. Detroit is most vulnerable against opposing tight ends, allowing the league's fifth-highest target share to the position, so this could be a game where the Bears finally get Colston Loveland going in a way that they haven't been able to accomplish as much as they likely wanted to this year. The Lions do limit yards after the catch better than any defense in the NFL, though, allowing only 4.0 YAC per completion, according to Tru Media. That could take away from some of Chicago's success in the screen game and possibly limit the effectiveness of Luther Burden III and — to a lesser extent because he's not as big a part of the offense — Kalif Raymond . When the Lions have the ball The Lions are third in the NFL in yards and fifth in points. They're fifth in both yards per play and points per drive, as well as fifth in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. They're second in EPA per pass attempt and third in EPA per rush attempt. They're third in passing success rate, first in rushing success rate and third in overall success rate. They are, in other words, a top-five offense by almost any measurement, and they can beat you with both the pass and the run. Jared Goff is having a marvelous season, completing 67.8% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt with 20 touchdown passes against six interceptions. He's third in the league behind only Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow in EPA per dropback, third behind only Purdy and Burrow in success rate and fourth behind only Purdy, Burrow and Patrick Mahomes in passer rating. His 8.2 yards-per-attempt average is the second-best of his tenure in Detroit, as are the 52.3% success rate and 107.7 passer rating. He's of course blessed with one of the best skill-position corps in the league: Amon-Ra St. Brown is a picture of consistency; Jameson Williams is one of the most explosive threats in football; Sam LaPorta is a strong option and tight end; and Jahmyr Gibbs is the best running back in the NFL, leading the league in rushes, rushing yards, first downs, yards from scrimmage and total touchdowns. St. Brown often gets pigeonholed as a slot guy, but in reality he plays more outside (59.2% of snaps) than he does inside (39.8%), according to Tru Media, and he's equally capable of dominating defenses from either spot. He's Goff's first read more often than not because he runs a lot of short-area routes and the Lions like to get the ball out fairly quickly in their straight dropback game, where St. Brown is often the target. Williams is the guy the Lions turn toward when they're looking to test defenses in the intermediate and deep areas of the field. His 12.36-yard average route depth is fourth among 199 players who have run 100 or more routes this season, according to Tru Media, and he's generated an explosive gain (16-plus yards) on 26.3% of his targets, which ranks 17th among that same group of players. He and LaPorta are generally going to eat into each other's target shares in any given week, while St. Brown remains the more consistent top target. The Bears' secondary is beatable, as Chicago ranks 22nd in net yards allowed per attempt, according to Pro-Football-Reference. Jaylon Johnson is not the same player he once was, Tyrique Stevenson is inconsistent, Kyler Gordon has barely played and Malik Muhammad has the ups and downs of a fourth-round rookie. If the Lions give Goff time to throw, he could feast on this group all afternoon. That's where Chicago's improved defensive line comes in. Since acquiring Jeffery Simmons, the Bears rank seventh in the league in EPA per dropback, per Tru Media, in large part because they have recorded a sack on 10.7% of opponent dropbacks. Prior to acquiring Simmons, Chicago's sack rate was 8.9%. That figure still ranked third in the league through seven weeks, but it's been much improved since the Bears dropped Simmons into the middle of the defensive line. Detroit is pretty strong up front, allowing pressure on only 32.3% of dropbacks, which ranks sixth in the NFL. The sack rate is a bit worse than that because Goff isn't the world's most mobile quarterback, but he's generally given adequate time to throw. The Lions' run game is diverse, efficient and explosive. Gibbs is seventh in the NFL in yards per carry, fifth in the share of runs that gain five or more yards and second in explosive run rate, according to Tru Media. home.blurb: There still is additional testing to be done, but if Bears fans are looking for a silver lining, the current belief is that Loveland could return later this season. Loveland got up and limped off the field on his own before visiting the blue medical tent, but he was eventually carted to the locker room and ruled out for the rest of the game. Loveland had one catch for 5 yards and lost a fumble at Ford Field. Chicago also already lost backup tight end Cole Kmet for the remainder of the season after he suffered a serious right knee injury in Week 7. So, that leaves tight ends Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson left to fill Loveland’s void until he can potentially return. After Thursday’s victory, Johnson said he did not yet know the severity of Loveland’s injury or whether it could end his season. “Nope, don’t know yet, no,” head coach Johnson told reporters. “We’ll find out.” The Bears coach also praised Roush and Carlson for stepping up in Loveland’s absence, saying they “did a phenomenal job.” The Bears selected Loveland with the No. 10 overall pick in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft out of Michigan. The Bears have some extra time to figure things out as they are scheduled to host the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 13 on December 6. The Chicago Bears were able to defeat the Detroit Lions 39-35 on Thanksgiving to secure their spot atop the NFC North at 9-2. However, the win may have come at quite the cost. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN , the knee injury that Bears tight end Colston Loveland suffered on Thursday is expected to land him on injured reserve and sideline him for at least four weeks. The Bears later said in a statement that “Colston Loveland is week-to-week with a knee injury.” Later Friday, Schefter updated his X post, stating, “Until Colston Loveland gets a second opinion on his knee injury, the Bears are not making any decisions about injured reserve, and he will be considered a week to week until then.” Loveland’s injury occurred on the Bears’ second offensive drive of the game. He got tangled up with with Lions linebackers Trevor Nowaske and Malcolm Rodriguez on the play and replays showed Lions defensive tackle Tyleik Williams pushing Loveland as he attempted to regain his balance. It’s certainly a blow to the Bears offense, nonetheless. Loveland looks like one of the league’s best up-and-coming playmakers after racking up 99 catches for 1,110 yards and nine touchdowns in his first two seasons in the league. With the Wolverines, Loveland recorded 117 catches for 1,466 yards and 11 touchdowns from 2022-24. He was also named first-team All-Big 10 in 2023 and second-team All-American in 2024. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams had his midsection examined after taking four sacks in Chicago’s win over Detroit. “Nothing showed up on the scans,” Williams said. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction for the Thanksgiving clash between NFC East rivals Kathryn Riley / Getty Images FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys (5-6) have the chance to do something they haven't done yet in the 2026 season against the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thanksgiving Day: win consecutive games. The only time the Cowboys have won back-to-back games under head coach Brian Schottenheimer came back in his first season in 2025 following their Week 10 bye. That was a stretch of three victories in a row against Las Vegas Raiders (33-16), the Eagles (24-21) and the Kansas City Chiefs (31-28) on Thanksgiving Day. After Dallas' 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans (1-9) on Sunday, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones has some hope that his squad can make a postseason push down the stretch. That's just days after Jones called his Cowboys "a bad team" in the wake of their 46-40 home loss against the San Francisco 49ers (9-1) in Week 10. "It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we wanted to do," Jones said postgame on Sunday. "We needed this kind of thing. Any team does. We needed to feel it and get a little wind under our wings, so to speak." Quarterback Dak Prescott looks to continue his high-level play on Thanksgiving. If he replicated his Sunday performance against the Titans (325 yards passing and four touchdowns on 28-of-33 passing with a rushing touchdown), that would give Prescott 19 passing touchdowns on Thanksgiving, the record for the most Thanksgiving Day touchdowns in NFL history. Prescott's predecessor Tony Romo and Matthew Stafford currently share the record with 18 Turkey Day passing touchdowns each. "It's a blessing. It's something that, one of my favorite games of the year," Prescott said Tuesday. "And so, just being able to put that uniform on with the John Madden seal on it, understanding the whole world's watching and how many little kids are in the position that I once was: watching the game and then ready to go outside and play my own version of it. ... I don't take it for granted." However, there's one Cowboy who doesn't look forward to Thanksgiving: defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . The four-time Pro Bowler doesn't enjoy the holiday because it goes against his in-season training and diet regimen. Williams' go-to Thanksgiving side dish is macaroni, something that is hard to resist this time of year. "It's during the season. I'm trying to stay lean and trim, and it's a holiday right around when real football starts to come in," said Williams. "So I'm not a big fan of Thanksgiving." That's okay, because there will be plenty of fans ready to see Williams on the field, especially against starting Eagles quarterback and former Cowboy Joe Milton. Dallas acquired Milton in a trade with the New England Patriots in April 2025, and he worked as one of Prescott's backups until the Eagles signed him off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 17. That's the same day Philadelphia placed Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) on injured reserve. "Haha, it's good to see him," said Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb . "I hope he don't go crazy." Let's dig into the matchup. Where to watch Cowboys vs. Eagles live Date: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 4:30 p.m. ET Location: AT&T Stadium (Arlington, Texas) TV: FOX | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Cowboys -8.5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Cowboys have the ball Prescott is cooking right now. He became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club. After racking up 1,003 yards passing, 11 touchdowns and just a single interception over the last three weeks, Prescott now ranks second in the league in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25). He also ranks eighth in touchdown-to-interception ratio (25-6) and passer rating (101.0) and fourth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.21) this season. Prescott credited his historic production to being able to play "balanced football" the last two weeks, with the Cowboys averaging the 12th-most rushing yards per game (125.5) since Week 10. "It really just opens up the whole playbook," Prescott said Thursday. "So it's a credit to all of it just, in that sense, coming together. Guys up front being physical in the run game, which then allows them to pass block a little bit easier there. And guys outside just getting open, making my job easier." In their 51-30 Week 11 win over the Titans, Schottenheimer provided Prescott and Co. their highest motion rate (63.5%) and play-action rate (58.3%) of the season, weeks after getting away from those staples through the first quarter of the year. Cowboys Pro Bowl wide receivers Lamb (1,108 receiving yards, the second most in the NFL) and George Pickens (780 receiving yards, the 11th most in the NFL) going up against the Eagles All-Pro cornerback tandem of Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean will be the key matchups on Thursday. However, Mitchell's status was uncertain because of a hamstring injury. The Eagles held walkthroughs on Monday and Tuesday, and they upgraded Mitchell to limited on Tuesday after he didn't participate on Monday. Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said Mitchell will be "fine" for Thanksgiving, and the Eagles listed him without a game status on the team's final injury report after he practiced fully on Wednesday, indicating he will indeed play. When the Eagles have the ball When the Eagles have the football, they'll definitely be looking to play ground-and-pound football with 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley . Barkley is currently on a streak of four consecutive games with a rushing touchdown, the longest streak of his career. The Cowboys have the worst run defense in football, allowing 151.5 rushing yards per game, and they struggle against Barkley's agile running style. Both Schottenheimer and Williams described Barkley as being a "jump cut" running back with how smoothly he can hit the hole and then glide to a different spot along the line of scrimmage and in the open field. Williams compared Barkley stylistically to Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving , who went off for 165 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in a 24-16 upset over the Cowboys in Week 5. Irving averaged a career-high 7.9 yards per carry that night at AT&T Stadium. Williams said the key is to stop Barkley's feet before he gets going. Williams also presents a challenge for Philadelphia as he leads the NFL with 18 tackles for loss, the most in a season by a defensive tackle since 2022. He also leads all defensive tackles in quarterback pressures (40) and co-leads his position in forced fumbles (4) along with Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter . Yet, he feels he can still find higher levels of play with the Cowboys defense allowing 20-plus points in 18 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the league. That's the longest such streak since the 2019-2021 Jacksonville Jaguars ' run of 25 straight games, per NFL Research . He completed 11 of his 21 throws for 141 passing yards while rushing for 7 yards on five carries. Prescott said he saw Milton develop most in Dallas on his mental side of the game and preparation as it pertains to pass protection adjustments and discernment at the line of scrimmage. "Joe is amazing, man. The athleticism that he has, the speed that he has, the arm talent that he has, he can do it all," Williams said. "So it's super dope to be able to go against him, especially after all the laughs and things we had in the locker room during training camp practices." The present iteration of the Eagles lacks the offensive artillery to win a duel with Prescott, Lamb and Pickens. That's especially true if Mitchell is unable to suit up on Thursday. Prescott is on a 20-game home winning streak against NFC East opponents, which is tied with Tom Brady (versus the AFC East) for the longest home winning streak by a starting quarterback against divisional opponents since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. He'll break the tie with Brady with his 21st such victory in a row on Thanksgiving. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Legendary quarterbacks close out the holiday slate in one of the biggest games of the season Getty Images The NFL's three-game Thanksgiving slate concludes with a blockbuster battle between two perennial playoff teams in the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs . A pair of franchises that have regularly butted heads during the Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes eras clash once again in one of the season's biggest showdowns to date. As is often the case when they square off in the regular season, there are significant postseason seeding implications at play in this showdown between the Bills and Chiefs. Buffalo stands in control of the AFC's No. 1 seed, while Kansas City is in a tightly contested race with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West crown and the top-four seed that comes with it. Should the Chiefs beat the Bills, not only would they solidify their standing in the division hunt, but they would also then give themselves a clear path to the top overall seed and a first-round bye. This game stands among the greatest Thanksgiving matchups in NFL history. The combined 17-3 record between the two teams is the second-best mark by win percentage entering a Thanksgiving game in the last 50 seasons. Both sides are also playing their best football of the season heading into the holiday duel. This is just the second game in league history to feature two teams riding three-game win streaks in which all of those victories came by 17 or more points. The only other such instance came in 2007 between Tom Brady's New England Patriots and Peyton Manning's Indianapolis Colts . The quarterback face-off in this contest is about as legendary as that one. Where to watch Bills vs. Chiefs live Date: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Highmark Stadium (Orchard Park, N.Y.) TV: NBC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook Bills vs. Chiefs key storylines Another Allen vs. Mahomes classic: A pair of all-time great quarterbacks have quite the history in head-to-head battles at this stage of their careers, and there is a sharp dichotomy between their records in regular-season matchups and playoff battles. While Allen owns a commanding 5-1 lead in the regular season, Mahomes has been dominant in win-or-go-home situations at 4-0. In games against each other, their passing numbers are nearly identical; Allen passed for 1,534 yards and 11 touchdowns to Mahomes' 1,552 yards and 10 touchdowns in their first 10 clashes. Where Allen owns a decided edge is in ball security (three interceptions vs. eight) and in rushing production (five touchdowns vs. zero). Top-tier running back showdown: Messaging out of Kansas City is that the Chiefs are hopeful Kenneth Walker III will return to action on Thursday following a two-game absence due to groin tightness. If he suits up, then the NFL is in for a tremendous running back battle. Walker (109.0) and Buffalo's James Cook III (106.0) rank second and third, respectively, in rushing yards per game and are in a race with Detroit Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs for the league rushing title. If Cook can return to the top of the leaderboard, he would pace the NFL in yardage for the second consecutive year. On Sunday, he set a new record for the most consecutive games (nine) with at least 75 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a season. Bills defense levels up: Over the first six games of the season, the Bills had to post gaudy scoring numbers in order to make up for a leaky defense. That was not the case in any of their last four games. All of a sudden, this unit ranks 11th in EPA per play allowed, has not surrendered more than 12 points in a game since Oct. 18 and is no longer a liability but rather an asset. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's unit has gone 15 quarters without allowing a touchdown, which is the NFL's longest single-season streak since 2000. The group still has to prove that it can play at this level against more formidable competition, though. Chiefs ride historic hot streak: Just like their upcoming opponent, the Chiefs enjoyed a stretch of games against lesser competition heading into the Thanksgiving battle and took care of business with ease. In routs of the New York Jets , Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals , the Chiefs tied the longest streak in franchise history of wins by at least 21 points (three). Even dating back to their last loss, Mahomes is in the midst of a scalding stretch with 13 passing touchdowns and no interceptions. Bills vs. Chiefs prediction It is difficult to knock Kansas City, because when it wins, it does so in resounding fashion and shows all the makings of a future Super Bowl winner. But the Chiefs' strength of schedule and results against projected playoff teams do raise questions about whether they can take down the Bills on the road in primetime. The Chiefs have only played three games against opponents with winning records all season and are just 1-2 in those contests. Both losses came on the road. Simply put, they have not shown an ability to win games like the one they are about to walk into. At the same time, the Bills defeated each of the three best teams on their schedule thus far. Plus, for whatever reason, Allen has Mahomes' number when they meet in the regular season. Add the defensive revival into the equation, and everything comes up Bills in this matchup. Awaiting them on Thanksgiving Day is one of their perceived top threats in the conference, the Buffalo Bills. In a classic tilt between all-world quarterbacks, dynamic head coaches and elite rushing attacks, many are calling for bushels of points on Thursday. On the other hand, an ugly weather report for the holiday may have different plans. With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 12 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: This has been true for a large number of Chiefs-Bills matchups in the past, but this game truly feels like a coin-flip. The loss of Kenneth Walker matters, but the Bills have unanswered questions on both sides of the ball. Buffalo wins these regular-season showdowns, but it’s arguably more important for Kansas City this time through. The Chiefs’ offensive tackles are cause for concern, but Patrick Mahomes has been playing tremendous football behind that same line for much of this season. James Cook is a weapon, but Steve Spagnuolo’s defense is typically stout against the run. Ultimately, this feels like a game that comes down to a late field goal or a fourth-quarter turnover. I’m relatively confident that this game will live up to the hype, but I could easily see either team escaping with the narrow victory. Jordan Foote: In my Week 12 preview, I echoed Brisco's sentiment and chalked this one up to a relative coin-flip as well. The Bills have plenty of holes on their roster and, in many ways, remind me of this Chiefs squad. Usually, having home-field advantage would be the deciding factor in a game like this, but Buffalo simply doesn't look like a club that's firing on all cylinders. The Kansas City defense will surely be put to the test against the dynamic rushing duo of Allen and Cook. There also may not be a more lethal play extender than Allen in the dropback game when he's operating at peak capacity. Still, the Chiefs have a running game of their own with Johnson enjoying some success. A heavy ball-control style of outing goes to KC. Expect a close one at the new Highmark Stadium. I'm not rolling with a combined 60-plus points, instead giving the visitors a one-score edge thanks to either a timely stop on defense or some Mahomes magic on the other side of the football. Joshua Schulman: The Chiefs are looking to change their fortunes against the Bills in the regular season. Patrick Mahomes may own Josh Allen in the postseason, but he’s 1-5 against Buffalo in regular-season meetings. With Kenneth Walker out for the third consecutive week, Emmett Johnson will take on a larger workload in his place. He’ll need to have a big day with cold temperatures and heavy rainfall expected in Buffalo. While the Chiefs have bounced back in a huge way since their two-game losing skid, they haven’t faced much competition. Behind Buffalo’s defense improved defense and a rowdy home crowd, I think it’ll be tough for the Chiefs to pull this one off. Tyler Brown: This is the kind of game that comes down to the last possession, and I think it ends up going Kansas City’s way despite Mahomes’ 1-5 record against Allen in the regular season. I think they match up that well. Allen is playing somewhat erratically, as shown by his nine touchdowns and nine interceptions over the past eight games. The Bills’ defense has looked great against backup quarterbacks, but it allows more than 30 points a game against good-to-average offenses, and Kansas City is as good as any. Mahomes has been dealing for a month, and he should find openings against a vulnerable defensive backfield. With Emmett Johnson carrying the load, the rushing attack will keep the Bills guessing. Travis Kelce, Josh Downs, and Rashee Rice can do the rest. It will not be easy to stop Allen, and you have to account for Cook as well. Allen always seems to find another gear against this team, and the Chiefs will have to keep him out of the red zone, where he is a touchdown vulture. But in a possible Thanksgiving shootout in the rain, I like the team that appears more balanced. The Chiefs have only one win against a team with a winning record, so this could be fool’s gold, but the process behind their recent surge looks legitimate.
